lyrics:
[Intro: stuttering machine kick, sequenced bass enters]

[Instrumental: synthetic choir chords, hi-hat]

[Verse 1: detached male voice]
Delivered at nine forty
Seen at nine forty-one
I watched the little word change
And then I watched it done

[Chorus: choir swells, bass octaves]
Tell me how it reads to you
Tell me what you saw
Seen at nine forty-one
And nothing more

[Instrumental: synth melody over the sequence]

[Verse 2: same flat delivery]
I count the hours after
I check the bars, the light
The phone is working perfectly
That's what's not right

[Chorus: choir swells, bass octaves]
Tell me how it reads to you
Tell me what you saw
Seen at nine forty-one
And nothing more

[Break: kick stutter alone, vocoder voice]
Seen. Seen. Seen.

[Outro: sequence and choir, slowly filtered away]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 130 BPM, 4/4, D minor. Cold, mechanical and danceable, with long instrumental stretches.

VOICE: Male, flat, untrained and detached, sung low with no vibrato, as if reading. One vocoder voice repeats a single word in the break.

INSTRUMENTS: A drum machine with a rapid sixteenth-note kick stutter, a sequenced octave synth bass, a sampled choir pad, a melodic bass guitar played high, a bright lead synth, hand claps, a vocoder.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, kick stutter. 0:16 Bass sequence. 0:40 Choir instrumental. 1:04 Verse 1. 1:28 Chorus 1. 1:52 Instrumental. 2:20 Verse 2. 2:44 Chorus 2. 3:08 Break, vocoder. 3:24 Outro, filtered away by 3:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1983 electronic dance: dry drum machine, analogue sequencer, cold digital choir, voice plain and central.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The opening kick stutter at 0:00.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original asks how it feels to be mistreated. The modern form of that question is a read receipt: proof you were seen, and nothing after.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Waiting, calculating, numb, unanswered.
